sources.title: Performance Audit Report on the Management of Floods
sources.organization: National Audit Office of Tanzania, Controller and Auditor General
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood-management audit covering 2020/21-2023/24; includes field observations and cited event reports from 2023-2024.
sources.methodology: Government performance audit combining interviews, records review and physical site observations in selected flood-prone local authorities.
sources.limitations: Visited local authorities were selected for flood exposure; results are not a representative survey of all councils.

sources.title: Water Sector Development Programme Phase III: Annual Water Sector Status Report 2024
sources.organization: United Republic of Tanzania, Ministry of Water
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-resource, rainfall and service delivery reporting for 2024, published March 2025.
sources.methodology: Annual ministry reporting on hydrology, water services, programme performance and implementation constraints.
sources.limitations: Annual basin and station summaries do not establish anthropogenic climate attribution or household-level impacts.

sources.title: Perceived existence of farmer-pastoralist conflicts in relation to climate change in Kilosa District, Tanzania
sources.organization: Emmanuel E. Chingonikaya and Farida Salehe; published by AkiNik Publications and hosted in the Sokoine University of Agriculture Institutional Repository
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 cross-sectional study of farmer-pastoralist relations in selected Kilosa wards and villages.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a cross-sectional design with 120 respondents, household surveys, focus groups and key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: Only the repository abstract was readable; no causal identification, conflict prevalence or ward-level results were available.

sources.title: Local governance and climate change adaptation: evidence from Monduli and Longido districts, Tanzania
sources.organization: Maeda, Namwata and Kumburu; Moshi Co-operative University Institutional Repository
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 mixed-methods study of local-authority adaptation implementation; study fieldwork dates not stated in the abstract.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a 351-member committee survey, 20 key-informant interviews and six focus groups.
sources.limitations: The full article PDF timed out; the abstract supplies no district-specific estimates or detailed measurement definitions.

sources.title: Climate adaptation in Tanzania's national budgeting process: embedding flood and drought preparedness
sources.organization: London School of Economics Grantham Research Institute and Behavioural Adaptation for Water Security and Inclusion project partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Eight-page August 2026 policy brief using 2025 interviews and national budget-cycle analysis.
sources.methodology: Multi-actor behaviour-journey analysis drawing on 43 purposively selected 2025 government and non-government interviews.
sources.limitations: National budgeting analysis, not a district impact evaluation; some budget shares are attributed to cited external reports.

sources.title: Enhancing the Adaptive Capacity of Semi-Arid Agropastoral Communities through Local Adaptation Plans in Dodoma
sources.organization: IKI Small Grants programme; implemented by the Forum on Climate Change (FORUMCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Completed project page for July 2023-August 2025; reports district planning and engagement outputs.
sources.methodology: Grant-programme page summarizes project context, implementation locations and implementer-reported outputs.
sources.limitations: Project-reported outputs and engagement; approved funding is not evidence of expenditure or independently evaluated impact.

claims.locator: Printed p. 59, section 3.4.2, citing the July 2024 Hanang post-landslide restoration report.
claims.paraphrase: The audit's cited July 2024 report says the 2023 Hanang mudslide affected 261 houses, destroyed 95, damaged 754.875 acres of farmland and disrupted 742 businesses.
claims.limitations: Event-specific totals are relayed from a district restoration report; this figure set does not establish climate attribution.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 58-63, sections 3.4.1-3.4.2 and photos 3.3(e)-(f), Kilosa site observation.
claims.paraphrase: In Kilosa, auditors observed a Standard Gauge Railway stormwater culvert without a continuous downstream channel; accumulated floodwater affected neighboring areas.
claims.limitations: September 2024 site observation; the audit attributes this instance to drainage obstruction, not climate change.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 37-38 and 53-54, sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.7; tables 3.2 and 3.6.
claims.paraphrase: In 2024, none of five visited councils had demarcated or protected identified flood-prone areas; the audit tables show no disaster-coordination allocations in Kinondoni, Hanang, Mbeya or Kilosa, unlike Rufiji.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Division
President's Office Regional Administration and Local Government
claims.limitations: Audit sample was selected for flood exposure; its narrative and table differ on the number of LGAs reviewed, so council-specific table entries are used.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 12-14, sections 3.1.1.1 and 3.1.1.3, Rufiji Basin rainfall and river-flow discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry reports Rufiji Basin rainfall at 169% of average in November 2023-March 2024; Great Ruaha flow at Msembe was 533.22 m3/s, 445% above its long-term average.
claims.limitations: These are basin and station hydrology observations for 2023-2024; the report does not attribute this anomaly to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 2-3 and 73-74, institutional roles and chapter 4 constraints.
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry assigns local water allocation to Water User Associations and rural-scheme operation to community water organizations; it reports staff, data, storage and financing gaps in 2024.
claims.limitations: The report lists sector-wide constraints and does not assess the capacity or service performance of named local associations.

claims.locator: Sokoine University repository abstract, methods and findings paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: A 2021 cross-sectional study of 120 respondents in selected Kilosa wards and villages reports farmer-pastoralist conflict over land, water and pasture and attributes resource scarcity partly to climate variability.
claims.limitations: Only the abstract was directly readable; the cross-sectional design does not identify causality, conflict prevalence or specific wards.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors conclude climate-change and variability-related scarcity of water, land and pasture contributes to farmer-pastoralist conflict in Kilosa.

claims.locator: Repository abstract, methods and results paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: A 2025 mixed-methods study across Monduli and Longido reports that responsiveness, accountability, transparency and stakeholder participation significantly influenced local adaptation implementation, with participation strongest.
claims.limitations: Abstract reports a 351-member survey plus interviews and focus groups but gives no district-specific estimates or detailed measures.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, national adaptation budgeting context and cited preparedness budget shares.
claims.paraphrase: The brief cites estimates that preparedness receives about 25% of the disaster-management budget, while the Water Ministry assigns about 6% to water-resource management versus 75% to water supply.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Department
claims.limitations: Budget shares are cited in the brief from 2023-2025 sources; they are not the brief's own fiscal audit.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 3-5, results of the 2025 interview and budget-cycle analysis.
claims.paraphrase: The 43-interview study identifies reactive-response norms, budget ceilings, institutional silos, weak coordination authority and generic monitoring as mutually reinforcing reasons flood and drought preparedness is underfunded.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Department
claims.limitations: Qualitative purposive interview findings concern national budget processes, not local flood- or drought-loss outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 5 and summary, proposed budget-cycle leverage points.
claims.paraphrase: The brief recommends preparedness rules in budget guidelines, costed and coordinated ministry plans, and transparent tracking of planned and actual preparedness spending.
claims.limitations: These are recommendations, not reported policy changes or completed preparedness investments.

claims.locator: IKI project page, initial situation and project-area description.
claims.paraphrase: The Dodoma project describes its Chamwino and Mpwapwa target communities as groundwater-dependent; unreliable rainfall affects crops and livestock and is associated with drought, flooding, erosion and limited recharge.
claims.limitations: The grant-programme description is regional and project-framed; it does not provide district-level hazard measurements.

claims.locator: IKI project page, completed-project status and key achievements.
claims.paraphrase: The completed project reports community-led plans adopted by Chamwino and Mpwapwa councils, 25 adaptation actions added to 2024/25 plans and budgets, and TZS 500 million approved for implementation.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported planning outputs and approved allocation; the page does not show disbursement or evaluated resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: IKI project page, target-group and engagement achievements.
claims.paraphrase: The project page lists 1,050 direct beneficiaries and a target group of 165 smallholder farmers, then reports 678 people engaged, equal to 64.5% of the target group.
geographies: project villages in Chamwino and Mpwapwa
claims.limitations: The denominator is the project's target group; listed direct beneficiaries are programme-reported reach, not independently verified outcomes.

search_audit.query: Tanzania subnational climate vulnerability district flood drought report primary source 2023 2024
search_audit.outcome: Read a national flood-management audit with impacts and infrastructure gaps in Hanang, Kilosa and other named councils; a ministry water report provides basin/station rainfall and river-flow observations; a completed Dodoma project page describes district risks and plans.

search_audit.query: Tanzania climate change conflict pastoralist farmer resource conflict climate security report primary research local districts
search_audit.outcome: A Sokoine-hosted 2021 study abstract explicitly attributes farmer-pastoralist conflict in Kilosa partly to climate variability and resource scarcity; access is abstract-only and its cross-sectional design cannot establish causality. A separate land-access paper's full text was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Tanzania conflict insecurity blocks climate adaptation flood drought response project access report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented conflict or insecurity blocking a named adaptation activity or climate response. Flood-management and local adaptation sources report institutional and resource constraints, not an FCV-to-climate pathway; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.

search_audit.query: Tanzania local climate resilience adaptation outcomes district community water irrigation restoration UN report 2023 2025
search_audit.outcome: Read local-adaptation governance findings for Monduli and Longido, Dodoma community adaptation-plan and budget outputs, Ministry of Water institutional constraints, and an LSE national preparedness-budget process study. Programme outputs and recommendations are distinguished from evaluated outcomes or completed reforms.

gaps: The only accessible study directly stating climate variability contributes to farmer-pastoralist conflict in Kilosa was a 2021 repository abstract; full text, named wards, conflict prevalence and causal identification were unavailable.
A separate study argues farmer-herder conflict in Rufiji and Kisarawe is shaped by pastoral land-access exclusion, but its publisher full text returned 403; it was not used as evidence.
No inspected source documented insecurity or violence preventing a named adaptation activity; local flooding preparedness gaps are not treated as FCV constraints.
Government flood audit figures are scoped to selected councils and 2020/21-2023/24; budget narrative and table differ on the number of reviewed local authorities.
MoCU's full local-governance study and the World Bank's 2026 climate-shock report were not readable; repository abstract or metadata alone do not provide district-level vulnerability estimates.
